portals.name: Ohio Court of Claims — Public Records Complaints
portals.covers: Formal complaints when a public office denies a records request or fails to respond. This is the cheap, fast alternative to a mandamus action.
portals.submission_notes: A special master is appointed and mediation is offered. Final orders may be appealed to the court of appeals for the district where the public office has its principal place of business (R.C. 2743.75(G)(1)).

portals.name: Ohio Revised Code (codes.ohio.gov)
portals.covers: Primary text of the Ohio Public Records Act and every other statute you will cite. Always quote from here, never from a summary.
portals.submission_notes: Section 149.43 is the Public Records Act. Section 2743.75 is the Court of Claims complaint process.

portals.name: Ohio Attorney General — Sunshine Laws / Yellow Book
portals.covers: The AG's annual Sunshine Laws manual — the standard reference public offices themselves are trained on. Quote it back to them.
portals.submission_notes: Cite the current edition by year and page when disputing a denial.

portals.name: Supreme Court of Ohio — Opinions & Case Search
portals.covers: Ohio Supreme Court opinions and dockets. Where you find the controlling public-records case law.
portals.submission_notes: Search by docket number, case title, or full text.

portals.name: Ohio Auditor of State — Audit Search
portals.covers: Released audit reports for ~5,000 units of Ohio government, including Findings for Recovery (public money not handled according to law).
portals.submission_notes: Findings for Recovery are the highest-value item here. Search by entity and year.

portals.name: Ohio Secretary of State — Business Entity Search
portals.covers: Every registered LLC, corporation, partnership, trade name and trademark in Ohio, with filed images. Core due-diligence lookup.
portals.submission_notes: Free, no registration. Pull the actual filing images, not just the summary screen — officers and agents are on the images.

portals.name: Franklin County Clerk of Courts — Case Information Online (CIO)
portals.covers: Common Pleas civil and criminal, Domestic Relations, and 10th District Court of Appeals cases.
portals.typical_fees: free to search; copy fees apply
portals.submission_notes: Search by party name or case number. You must accept a disclaimer page first. Phone: 614-525-3600.

portals.name: Franklin County Municipal Court Clerk — Case Search
portals.covers: Municipal court cases: misdemeanors, traffic, evictions, small claims. This is where most local police charges land.
portals.submission_notes: Search by case or ticket number for best results; name search also works.

portals.name: Columbus City Council — Legistar
portals.covers: Full ordinance, resolution, agenda and minutes history for Columbus City Council. Where ordinances like 3142-2023 and 1075-2024 live.
portals.submission_notes: Search by ordinance number or keyword; export result lists. Attachments hold the contracts.

portals.name: City of Columbus — Public Records Request
portals.covers: Central intake for City of Columbus records requests, including Department of Public Utilities.
portals.submission_notes: Route DPU rate and consent-order questions here and ask them to confirm the custodian in writing.

portals.name: Franklin County Auditor — Property Search
portals.covers: Parcel ownership, valuation, transfers, and tax history. Primary tool for property due diligence.
portals.submission_notes: Search by address, owner, or parcel ID. Transfer history shows the chain of ownership.

portals.name: Franklin County Recorder — Official Records Search
portals.covers: Deeds, mortgages, liens, easements, UCC filings. Where you prove who actually owns and who is owed.
portals.submission_notes: Search by name or instrument number. Certified copies cost extra.

portals.name: City of Gahanna — Public Records Request
portals.covers: City of Gahanna records intake, including police department reports, body-worn camera footage, and dispatch/CAD records.
portals.submission_notes: Body-worn camera requests are their own category under R.C. 149.43(A)(17) restricted-portion rules — ask for the unredacted-to-you portions and get any withholding cited in writing.

portals.name: City of Reynoldsburg — Public Records Request
portals.covers: Reynoldsburg records intake — water/wastewater billing, council, service department.
portals.submission_notes: Email publicrecords@reynoldsburg.gov. Carried over from your v0.5 seed set.

portals.name: Ohio EPA — eDocument Search
portals.covers: Ohio EPA permits, findings and orders, and correspondence. Where consent orders and Director's Final Findings & Orders are filed.
portals.submission_notes: Search by facility or document type. Director's Final Findings & Orders are the primary documents behind the consent-order language in the sewer ordinances.

portals.name: Ohio Water Development Authority
portals.covers: OWDA loan applications, board minutes, and the state loan portfolio for water/sewer projects.
portals.submission_notes: Board minutes are posted; the full loan portfolio usually requires a records request.

portals.name: Ohio Secretary of State — Campaign Finance
portals.covers: Contribution and expenditure filings for state candidates, PACs, and committees. Follow the money into the decision.
portals.submission_notes: County boards of elections hold local candidate filings that never reach the state system — request those separately.

portals.name: Ohio Ethics Commission — Financial Disclosure
portals.covers: Annual financial disclosure statements for Ohio public officials. Shows outside income, creditors, and conflicts.
portals.submission_notes: Statements are generally obtainable on request; the requester's identity may be disclosed to the filer in some circumstances — confirm before filing.

portals.name: PACER — Federal Court Records
portals.covers: All federal district, bankruptcy, and appellate dockets and filings.
portals.typical_fees: $0.10 per page, $3.00 cap per document; fees waived if quarterly usage stays under the threshold
portals.submission_notes: Use the free CourtListener/RECAP mirror first to avoid paying for documents someone already pulled.

portals.name: CourtListener / RECAP Archive
portals.covers: Free mirror of federal court documents already pulled from PACER, plus state appellate opinions.
portals.submission_notes: Always check here before spending PACER money.

portals.name: USAspending.gov
portals.covers: Federal contracts, grants, and loans by recipient. Good for tracing federal money into local projects.
portals.submission_notes: Search by recipient name and by place of performance.

portals.name: SAM.gov — Entity & Exclusions Search
portals.covers: Federal contractor registration and the exclusions (debarment) list. Check every contractor here.
portals.submission_notes: The exclusions list is the fast red-flag check in any vendor due-diligence pass.

portals.name: Columbus Metropolitan Library — Public Records Request
portals.covers: Columbus Metropolitan Library system records: board minutes, budgets, policies, contracts, branch records.
portals.submission_notes: CML is its own public office with its own records custodian. Do NOT route library requests through the City of Columbus — the city is not the custodian and the request will die there.

portals.name: FEC — Campaign Finance Data
portals.covers: Federal candidate, committee and PAC filings: who gave, to whom, how much. Free API at api.open.fec.gov with a key from api.data.gov.
portals.submission_notes: The API is the fast path — see modules/connectors (fec). Individual contributions are schedule_a; independent expenditures are schedule_e.

portals.name: U.S. Senate — Lobbying Disclosure
portals.covers: Quarterly federal lobbying filings: which firm is paid by which client, how much, and on which bills. Free API, optional key.
portals.submission_notes: Registrant is the lobbying firm; client is who pays. The issue codes tell you the subject matter. Cross-reference against FEC for the same client.

portals.name: Ohio Joint Legislative Ethics Committee — Lobbying
portals.covers: Ohio legislative and executive agency lobbyist registrations and expenditure reports. The state-level counterpart to the Senate LDA.
portals.submission_notes: This is where Ohio Statehouse lobbying lives. No public API — search the web portal and file a records request for bulk data.

portals.name: County Board of Elections — Local Campaign Finance
portals.covers: LOCAL candidate and issue-committee campaign finance filings: county commissioners, city council, school board, township trustees, levy committees.
portals.submission_notes: THE gap in every API. Local candidate filings never reach the Ohio SOS system and are not in FEC. You must go to the county BOE directly — in person or by records request. One BOE per county.

portals.name: Ohio Checkbook — State Expenditures
portals.covers: State of Ohio spending by vendor, agency and category. Local governments participate voluntarily, so coverage below the state level is uneven.
portals.submission_notes: Good for tracing a vendor across state agencies. Absence here does NOT mean absence of payment — check the entity's own records too.
